question: T12 (task-a2e5696bd448c54b): on the desktop, a one-step fall of Wave Intensity (180 to 150, a 30 px fall of the line, under a row) on a Scrolling block made taller by hand than its line needs: how many rows does it keep, and does a Text block that starts between the new and the old foot follow it up? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10). Then 'open' (select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design), a press on Wave Intensity at the range's end (180: 1/2/7/26), 'go' (Escape and a press on the page); 'place i r0/c0/r1/c1' moves and resizes block i by hand: the Scrolling block to 1/2/12/26 (11 rows, its line needs 6), and the Text block to 8/2/13/10 (L1, ending under the old foot), 8/2/12/10 (L2, ending on it) or 6/2/12/10 (L3). Then 'open', a press on 150, 'go', and Cmd+Z until as built. R1 and R2 are two sessions (oracleW's probe-w.mjs), each ran L1 to L3 with other plans of other tasks. Exit without saving each time.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, the range's value). The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: L1, L2 and L3 alike: 150 takes the Scrolling block from 1/2/12/26 to 1/2/11/26, one row, its height less the line's fall snapped to the row pitch (441 px less 30 leaves 10 rows), as a fall of two steps or more does (CAP-T12WAVEDROP); not to the 5 rows that hold the new 184 px line. The section keeps 12 rows.
The Text block stays where it was placed in all three: 8/2/13/10, 8/2/12/10 and 6/2/12/10. Each starts above the new foot (11), so the desktop fall rule leaves it.

The press is one undo step: Escape keeps every area, and the first Cmd+Z gives back 1/2/12/26 with the Text block where it was; the next ones take back the places one by one. R1 and R2 read alike in every read (areas, rows, line, Undo and Redo).
Not read: a drag or a key through the same step, a block made taller by hand by less or more rows, a Text block that starts under the new foot, the phone view.
